items.title: Candido Camero — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: My dad taught me to play the tres.

ctx.x: Maestro to some extent you had a very productive childhood in a musical sense. Now, you told me that you began playing professionally at fourteen. But before we get to that point, tell us about that stage of practice, rehearsal, and daily discipline that eventually prepared you to play professionally. Tell me more stories about the influence of your father as a musician, of your uncle who was also as a musician. Tell me about that musical training. Your mother as a singer and because - we started to go there.

Well, as I said earlier, my uncle taught me to play the bongos starting when I was four, but as an amateur. My dad taught me to play the tres. My mother played in the community and at home and I would sing the chorus for her and stuff. Now the other uncles from my mom’s side, they were all musicians. One taught me to play the bass as a hobby.
